questions.question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Get into hot water
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'** i.e. **'To get into trouble'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Get into hot water"** is an English idiom that means **"to get into trouble".**
 
• **It refers** to finding oneself in a difficult or precarious situation.
 
• The phrase originated from the idea that hot water can burn or scald, implying danger or trouble.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: ***'To get into trouble'.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's examine all the options one by one:
 
 
• **To get a costly gift: **This option does not align with the idiom. Getting a costly gift is generally considered a positive event (महंगा उपहार पाना)
 
• **To reach nowhere:** This suggests that no progress or achievement has been made.(कहीं नहीं पहुंचना) It doesn't align with the meaning of the idiom.
 
• **A private end to serve:** This phrase implies having a personal or private goal to achieve, often in a somewhat selfish or secretive manner.(निजी उद्देश्य की सेवा करना)

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

More than 40 percent of the world’s population lives in regions where water has becoming increasingly scarce.

options.text: More than 40 percent of the world’s population

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence contains an **error in option 1**: "has becoming increasingly scarce".
 
• The** problem lies** in the **verb tense.**
 
• **In English,** the **present perfect tense** is** formed by** using "has" or "have" followed by a past participle (in most cases, a verb ending in -ed).
 
• The verb **"become" **should be used in its past participle form, "become", not "becoming".
 
• The phrase should be corrected to** "has become increasingly scarce".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* "More than 40 percent of the world’s population lives in regions where water has become increasingly scarce."*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

He said, “You were making excuses.”

options.text: He said that I had been making excuses.
He said that you were making excuses.
He said that you had been making excuses.
He said that I was making excuses.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **correct indirect form** of the given sentence is **option 1: **"He said that I had been making excuses."
 
• In reported speech, if the reporting verb (like "said" in this case) is in the past tense, then **we usually shift the tenses back **in the reported clause.
 
• When, the given direct sentence is in **'Past continuous tense'** , the indirect sentence will be** changed** to **'Past perfect continuous tense'**.
 
• **'Were' **will be changed into **'Had been'.**
 
• **'You'** will be changed into **'I'.**

Therefore, the **correct answer** is:* 'He said that I had been making excuses.'*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

My father cooks breakfast every day.

options.text: Breakfast was being cooked every day by my father.
Breakfast was cooked every day by my father.
Breakfast is cooked every day by my father.
Breakfast was cook every day by my father.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct passive form** of the sentence is **option 3:*** "Breakfast is cooked every day by my father."*
 
• In the original sentence, **"My father"** is the subject, **"cooks"** is the verb in simple present tense, and **"breakfast"** is the object. 
 
• **When we convert **this into the passive voice, the object ("breakfast") becomes the subject, the verb ("cooks") changes to its past participle form ("cooked"), and the original subject ("my father") is preceded by "by". 
 
• **We also use "is" **before the verb to keep it in the present tense, resulting in "Breakfast is cooked every day by my father."

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *'Breakfast is cooked every day by my father.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's go through all the options:
 
 
• **"Breakfast was being cooked every day by my father." **This is incorrect because it uses the past continuous tense ("was being cooked") instead of the simple present tense.
 
• **"Breakfast was cooked every day by my father."** This is incorrect because it uses the simple past tense ("was cooked") instead of the simple present tense.
 
• **"Breakfast was cook every day by my father."** This is incorrect due to the grammatical error "was cook" and the use of the past tense "was".

The correct answer is **'option 1' **i.e. **"discovered".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In the context **of this sentence, the team of scientists has mapped the seabed and found something that resembles an asteroid impact crater.
 
• The word **"discovered" **fits best here, as it denotes the action of finding something unexpected or previously unknown.

Therefore, the correct sentence is: *The ocean floor is famously less explored than the surface of Mars. And when our team of scientists recently mapped the seabed, and ancient sediments beneath, we **discovered** what looks like an asteroid impact crater. Intriguingly, the crater, (3)______ “Nadir” after the nearby volcano Nadir Seamount, is of the same age as the Chicxulub impact caused by a huge asteroid at the end of the Cretaceous (4)______, around 66 million years ago, which (5)______ the dinosaurs and many other species.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's consider the other options:
 
 
• **"Screened"** generally means to view or examine something, but in this context, it doesn't capture the idea of finding something new or unexpected.
 
• **"Shaped"** means to give a particular shape or form to something, but this doesn't fit the context here as the scientists aren't creating or forming the asteroid impact crater.
 
• **"Founded"** refers to establishing or setting up an institution or organization, which doesn't fit in the context of this sentence as the scientists are finding something, not setting up an organization.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'option 2'** i.e.** "named".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In this context,** the crater has been given a specific name, "Nadir," after the nearby volcano, Nadir Seamount.
 
• Thus**, "named" **is the most suitable word to fill in the blank.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *The ocean floor is famously less explored than the surface of Mars. And when our team of scientists recently mapped the seabed, and ancient sediments beneath, we discovered what looks like an asteroid impact crater. Intriguingly, the crater, **named** “Nadir” after the nearby volcano Nadir Seamount, is of the same age as the Chicxulub impact caused by a huge asteroid at the end of the Cretaceous (4)______, around 66 million years ago, which (5)______ the dinosaurs and many other species.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Let's consider the other options:
 
 
• **"Dropped"** generally means to let or make (something) fall vertically. It does not fit here because the sentence is about giving a name to the crater, not about dropping something.
 
• **"Murmured"** usually refers to a soft, low, or indistinct sound made by a person or group of people speaking quietly or at a distance. It does not fit in the given context.
 
• **"Squeaked"** means to make a short, high-pitched sound or cry. This also doesn't make sense in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'option 3'** i.e.** "period".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a geological or historical context, the word **"period"** is used to denote a span of time characterized by specific conditions, events, or forms of life.
 
• Here, the** "Cretaceous"** refers to a specific geologic time period, making "period" the appropriate term.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *The ocean floor is famously less explored than the surface of Mars. And when our team of scientists recently mapped the seabed, and ancient sediments beneath, we discovered what looks like an asteroid impact crater. Intriguingly, the crater, named “Nadir” after the nearby volcano Nadir Seamount, is of the same age as the Chicxulub impact caused by a huge asteroid at the end of the Cretaceous **period**, around 66 million years ago, which (5)______ the dinosaurs and many other species.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's consider the other options:
 
 
• **"Generation" **refers to all of the people born and living at about the same time, regarded collectively. It doesn't fit the context here because the Cretaceous is a geological era, not a generation of people.
 
• **"Spell"** could refer to a period of time, but it's usually used to denote a shorter, definite period of time, often with a specific characteristic, like a dry spell or a spell of good weather. It's not used to refer to geological eras.
 
• **"Vase"** is a container for holding flowers or for decoration, and it doesn't make sense in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'option 1' **i.e.** "wiped out".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, **"wiped out"** is the most appropriate phrase. It means to completely destroy or eliminate.
 
• **We know from** historical data that the Chicxulub impact around 66 million years ago was a significant event that led to the extinction of dinosaurs and many other species.
 
• Therefore, the phrase **"wiped out"** aptly describes the impact's effect on these species.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *The ocean floor is famously less explored than the surface of Mars. And when our team of scientists recently mapped the seabed, and ancient sediments beneath, we discovered what looks like an asteroid impact crater. Intriguingly, the crater, named “Nadir” after the nearby volcano Nadir Seamount, is of the same age as the Chicxulub impact caused by a huge asteroid at the end of the Cretaceous period, around 66 million years ago, which** wiped out** the dinosaurs and many other species.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's consider the other options:
 
 
• **"Absolved in"** usually refers to being freed from guilt or blame. This does not fit the context because the impact didn't absolve or free the dinosaurs, it caused their extinction.
 
• **"Turned off"** can refer to the action of stopping the operation of something. It is not appropriate here because it does not adequately convey the effect of the asteroid impact on the dinosaurs.
 
• **"Counted in"** usually means to include someone or something in an activity or process. This phrase does not fit the context of the sentence because the impact didn't count the dinosaurs in; instead, it led to their extinction.
